newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica business sees soft landing, rate cut later.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica business sees soft landing, rate cut later.

text.p: South Africa's economy should experience a soft landing rather than recession in 1997, despite a surprise drop in first quarter GDP, the South African Chamber of Business (Sacob) said on Thursday.

There was scope for at least one interest rate cut of one percentage point by the end of the year, provided the July 1 easing of exchange controls on individuals passed without any major impact on the rand, it added.

"In spite of the recent figures indicating negative growth in the first quarter, the economy still seems set to achieve a soft landing in the year ahead with a GDP growth rate of around 2.5 percent in 1997," Sacob said in presenting its monthly business confidence index.
GDP fell a seasonally adjusted and annualised 0.8 percent in the quarter to March from the fourth quarter of 1996, confounding economists who had forecast a rise of 2.5 percent.
But a large part of the fall was due to a quarterly slump in agriculture, and Sacob noted that compared to the first quarter of 1996 GDP had still advanced 2.4 percent.
This suggested that that a recession -- or three successive quarters of negative growth -- was most unlikely, Sacob said.

The organisation also took comfort from annualised growth in manufacturing output of 3.6 percent in the first quarter, on the back of strong exports, which suggested manufacturing would be the mainstay of the economy in 1997.
Commenting on interest rate prospects, Sacob said:

"If July's exchange control liberalisation does not have a large negative impact on the rand, then pressure on the Reserve Bank to maintain high interest rates will be eased. Sacob is still of the opinion that interest rates should be cut by at least one percent by the year end."
